rationale: OFI and HD are both maximal: intake lists four named requirements with stop-on-missing-item, and the HOLD table enumerates distinct named conditions each with a prescribed return instead of a guess. DBC 9: fast-path pruning, stack-reuse, silent decision-eval skip, and scope refused at write; cut logic is policy, not a live scan. NRC 9: refuse list (plan-as-product, auto-approval, unverifiable-as-pass, general-purpose on matched work, unfalsifiable blockers) plus three-state verification as the output test. RWR 9 (was 7): nine-step method card is self-contained; companion binding HOLDs when a later agent is handed only a sibling skill; dispatcher must log 'decided nothing'. MT 9: the card is step-indexed and readable; specialist rows and the type-conflict table still live in the orchestrator. OEA 8: names gate:product, specialist framing, approval-level, second-model verification, vertical vocabulary, and cost-attribution as distortions, plus what still needs a human. Composite 93.0, no HOLD, no veto — admit on the instrument. PRIME stopgate: not copied into skills/, not committed, not pushed.
